column1: # A test of how complete the People's Daily database of Xi Jinping's speeches and activities (jhsjk.people.cn) is, made on Nov 24, 2026: 156 items of Xi's, dated Feb 1, 2023 to Nov 20, 2026, taken from OUTSIDE the database (Xinhua's lists of his activities and the contents of Qiushi's issues) because their text holds a word on chips, computing power, AI, American firms or curbs, and each then looked for in the database by the database's own exact search. Result: the database holds 150 and lacks 6, his meeting of May 14, 2026 with the American executives and five joint statements. Which items: 75 Xinhua items picked by the words of their titles and 22 lead articles of Qiushi (keys s and q), all with such a word in the text; then, of 1,512 further Xinhua items read in full, the 38 with a word other than 人工智能 (AI) and every eighth of the 124 whose only such word is 人工智能 (16 items; keys r); and five joint statements from among those 124 (keys ending in j). So 21 of the 124 were checked (16 and 5) and 103 were not; near-duplicates of one event were dropped from the first 97. Columns: key; the item's date in the outside list; its title there; the words found in its text; the verdict (HELD = the search returned an item dated from 2 days before to 10 days after the item whose title shows it is the same item, read by eye; NOT HELD otherwise); the database's article numbers of the hits; how the verdict was reached (automatic = by the phrase quoted; by hand = by a second search, described); what the project's own dated list of Xi's statements holds within three days of the item (date, theme and saved id of each entry, or -; that list is a working note and is not published); and the item's address outside the database. What the table is not: not a list of everything Xi said or did; a HELD verdict says that the database has the item, not what the item says; and the searches of the database for Nvidia and for words on buying chips are in tables/xi_searches.tsv, not here.
